title: Cleisthenes and Democracy
objective: After this level you can explain how Cleisthenes created democracy in 508 BCE.
summary: After the tyrants fell, Cleisthenes (508-507 BCE) mixed Attica into ten new tribes and a Council of 500 chosen by lot: the start of demokratia.

cards.headline: In 508 BCE, one Athenian reshuffled every citizen in Attica.
cards.body: It sounds like paperwork. It’s the moment Athenian democracy began. First, how Athens got there.

cards.headline: From tyrants to a showdown
cards.body: After Solon, Athens fell under tyrants: Peisistratus, then his son Hippias. In 510 BCE the Spartan king Cleomenes marched in and expelled Hippias. Then two nobles fought for control. Isagoras, backed by Sparta, won the top office in 508, but his rival Cleisthenes had the people on his side. When Cleomenes came back to support Isagoras, the Athenians forced them both out.

cards.headline: Shuffle the deck
cards.body: Cleisthenes replaced Athens’ four old tribes, based on descent, with ten new ones. He split Attica into three zones (the city, the coast and the inland) and gave every tribe townships, called demes, from all three. Your rights now came from your deme, which kept its own list of citizens. Like sorting a school into teams that each mix every class, it made tribes less likely to follow local and family loyalties.

cards.headline: People power, by lottery
cards.body: Each tribe sent 50 men to a new Council of 500. Councillors had to be at least 30 and were chosen by lot every year, and the Council prepared the proposals the Assembly voted on. Cleisthenes is regarded as the founder of Athenian democracy. The word came a little later: demokratia, from demos (people) and kratos (rule), was coined in the middle of the 5th century BCE.

mascot.line: A council picked by drawing lots. Imagine your name coming up in the civic raffle!

cards.headline: Cleisthenes: founded
learned: Ten new tribes mixed city, coast and inland
A Council of 500 chosen by lot

questions.prompt: How many members sat on the Council that Cleisthenes built from his ten tribes?

options.rationale: Far too many: ten tribes sent 50 each.

questions.explanation: Each of the ten tribes sent 50 councillors, chosen by lot: the Council of 500.

questions.prompt: Why did Cleisthenes build each new tribe from demes in the city, on the coast and inland?

options.label: To keep each old family group in one tribe
options.rationale: He broke up the old descent-based tribes.

options.label: To mix Athenians from all over Attica together
To give Sparta a seat in each tribe
To make each tribe a separate city-state
options.rationale: The tribes were parts of one Athens.

questions.explanation: Mixing city, coast and inland in every tribe made tribes less likely to follow local and family loyalties.

questions.prompt: Level 21 showed that Athens ruled all of Attica. How did Cleisthenes use that whole region?

options.label: He gave each town its own king
options.rationale: Athens had just expelled its tyrant.

options.label: He moved everyone into the city
He built tribes mixing city, coast and inland
He handed the coast to Sparta

questions.explanation: Because Attica was one city-state, Cleisthenes could mix townships from all three of its zones into each new tribe.
